topic: Cities, lakes and islands of Britain

payload.title: Cities, lakes and islands of Britain

explanations.Bristol: A city and ceremonial county in south-west England.
explanations.Dundee: The fourth-largest city in Scotland, on the Firth of Tay.
explanations.Cardiff: The capital and largest city of Wales.
explanations.Windermere: The largest lake in England, in the Lake District.
explanations.Loch Ness: A large freshwater loch in the Scottish Highlands.
explanations.Bala Lake: The largest natural lake in Wales, known in Welsh as Llyn Tegid.
explanations.Isle of Wight: An island off the south coast of England.
explanations.Isle of Skye: The largest island of the Inner Hebrides, in Scotland.
explanations.Anglesey: The largest island in Wales, off its north-west coast.

sources.excerpt: Bristol is a city and ceremonial county in South West England.
Dundee is the fourth-largest city in Scotland.
Cardiff is the capital and largest city of Wales.

Windermere (historically Winder Mere) is a ribbon lake in Cumbria, England. It is within the Lake District and is the largest lake in England by length, area, and volume, although considerably smaller than the largest Scottish lochs and Northern Irish loughs.
Loch Ness is a large freshwater loch in the Scottish Highlands.
Llyn Tegid, also known as Bala Lake or Lake Bala in English, is a large freshwater glacial lake in Gwynedd, Wales.
The Isle of Wight is an island off the south coast of England.
The Isle of Skye, or simply Skye, is the largest and northernmost of the major islands in the Inner Hebrides of Scotland.
Anglesey, or Ynys Môn, is an island off the north-west coast of Wales.

editorNotes: Every tile lies in one of the three countries only, and none crosses a row either. Windermere is a lake rather than the town of the same name on its shore, and it is in Cumbria, not in Scotland or Wales; Loch Ness is a Highland loch and so a Scottish lake; Bala Lake is the English name of Llyn Tegid in Gwynedd. The Isle of Wight is an English ceremonial county, Skye is in the Inner Hebrides and Anglesey is a Welsh county, so no island can move column. Bristol, Dundee and Cardiff are cities and not lakes or islands. I considered Holy Island for an island that could sit in two columns, since there is one in Northumberland and another off Anglesey, but those are two different places sharing a name rather than one island in two countries, so I left it out. With every tile satisfying exactly one cell, there is only one valid placement.
